# PaceLine how-to guides

Task guides for PaceLine. Each guide says when you need it, the steps, and how to tell it worked.
Type the `/paceline:` commands in a session. Run the `paceline` commands in a session's Bash tool,
or ask the agent to run them. The [reference](reference.md) lists every option. The guides for
context-watch and cache-watch, which moved to the PitCrew plugin, are in [PitCrew's how-to
guides](../../pitcrew/docs/how-to.md).

## The night queue moved to the Stint plugin

**When you need it:** you want the agent to work through a list of tasks while you are away, within
what the week can spare.

The night queue moved to the Stint plugin: install it with `/plugin install stint@agentpit`, queue
items with `stint add` or `/stint:queue`, and run them with `/stint:run`. Stint obeys `paceline
advice`, which keeps the budget, the agent count and the stops of this plugin in force. `paceline
queue` and `paceline auto` print where they went and exit with status 2.

## Plan a week

**When you need it:** you want the budget to follow how heavy each day will be: a day off, a light
day, a long one.

1. See the week. Each day has two parts, its working hours (☼) and the off-hours after them (☾);
   each has a mark and a share of what is left:

   ```
   paceline plan
   ```

   A mark is `off`, `light`, `normal`, `heavy`, or a number from 0 to 2 in steps of 0.25. Working
   hours are `normal` and off-hours `off` until you mark them. `◀ now` shows the part that is
   running and what it has spent against its share.
2. Mark a day. A day is `today`, `tomorrow`, `mon` to `sun`, or a date; it must be a day of the
   current week:

   ```
   paceline plan set fri --work off
   paceline plan set tomorrow --work heavy --off-hours light
   ```

   A part's share is fixed when the part starts. A mark for the part that is running splits it at
   once: the part ends now and keeps its share and spending, and the rest starts now with a share
   from what is left of the week by the new mark (while the away marker is on, the part is not split
   and the command says so). A mark for a part that has ended is stored but changes nothing this
   week; the parts after the running one follow the new marks at once. In a terminal tab of Claude
   Code Desktop, which has no session, the commands that write (`plan set`, `plan reset`, `mode
   inform`, `mode limit`) refuse with `account not known yet (desktop)`: run them from a session's
   Bash, or set `PACELINE_ACCOUNT_KEY` to the key that `paceline status --json` shows as
   `data.account.key` there.

   In Claude Code Desktop, open `/paceline:settings pane` and choose Calendar: a card per day of the
   week with its title, its ☼ and ☾ marks and their shares, and a bar on a grey track: the bar runs
   to the bar top and the grey is the room left. A part that has ended shows what it spent, or `not
   recorded` when the plan holds no spend for it. The days that have ended fold into one line that
   unfolds when pressed. − and + change the mark of a part that has not ended, through `paceline
   plan set`; a change to the part that is running splits it at that moment. The ended parts show
   their marks without buttons. On a phone the tab is read-only.
3. Mark a weekday for every week with the template, and remove a day's marks:

   ```
   paceline plan template set mon --work heavy
   paceline plan reset fri
   ```

4. To change the working hours, run `paceline profile set work_hours 08:00-17:00`, or use the
   Working hours row of `/paceline:settings pane` (− and + move each end by 15 minutes). The new
   hours apply from the end of the part that is running.
5. To choose what a plan does, run `paceline mode limit` (a launch asks first when the current part
   is more than 1 point over its share pro rata) or `paceline mode inform` (the default: it only
   shows). In `limit`, `paceline mode inform --until-part-end` stops the questions until the current
   part ends.

**How to tell it worked:** On Tuesday at 09:00, 79% is left after the reserve. Tuesday is `heavy`
(1.5), and the marks from Tuesday on add up to 5, so Tuesday's working hours get 79 × 1.5 / 5 =
23.7%. `paceline plan` at 11:30 shows that share with `spent 2.0 of 23.7`.

## Keep a reserve for a task at the end of the week

**When you need it:** a task such as a test run must still fit on Friday, and you do not want the
week's other work to use up the allowance first.

1. Set the size, the weekday it opens on, and a name. The reserve keeps 10% of the week out of the
   plan and out of launches until Friday's working hours begin:

   ```
   paceline reserve 10 --release fri --name tests
   ```

   The answer prints the change and the reserve's text, for example `reserve "tests" 10 % kept,
   opens Fri 30 09:00`. Until then a launch asks once the week's usage reaches 90%; from the release
   the 10% is spread over the rest of the week like the rest. Check it at any time with `paceline
   reserve`, `paceline status` or `paceline plan`.
2. To change it later, give only what changes: `paceline reserve 12`, `paceline reserve --release
   last` (the last day before the reset, the default), or `paceline reserve --name ""` to clear the
   name. `paceline reserve 0` turns the reserve off and keeps the day and name. The settings pane
   has the same three rows under Weekly reserve.

## Keep usage current while idle

**When you need it:** you want pace and status line plugins to show the exact figures `/usage`
shows, including the model-scoped weekly limits, while no session makes requests.

**Before you turn it on:** usage-watch is off until you run `/paceline:usage-watch on`. It reads
`https://api.anthropic.com/api/oauth/usage`, an endpoint outside Anthropic's published API
reference, through Claude Code with the session's own login; its address, answer format, or
availability can change without notice. It needs a claude.ai login and an open session with
PaceLine, pauses while the computer sleeps, and sends nothing while
`CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_NONESSENTIAL_TRAFFIC` is set. When the endpoint fails, `/paceline:usage-watch
status` shows `last error: HTTP <status>` or `unexpected response`, PitBoard's model-scoped limits
disappear after 15 minutes, and pace's model-scoped rules stop applying. Without usage-watch, the
limits writer, the five-hour and weekly readings from each session's turns, pace's budget, and the
advice keep working, with data as of the last turn. The [limitations](limitations.md#usage-watch)
list each case: [the login](limitations.md#limit-readings-need-a-claudeai-subscription-login), [off
by default](limitations.md#usage-watch-is-off-by-default), [the
endpoint](limitations.md#usage-watch-reads-an-endpoint-outside-the-published-api), [an open
session](limitations.md#usage-watch-needs-an-open-session),
[sleep](limitations.md#a-sleeping-computer-pauses-usage-watch), and [the traffic
setting](limitations.md#claude_code_disable_nonessential_traffic-blocks-usage-watch).

1. Turn usage-watch on:

   ```
   /paceline:usage-watch on
   ```

   The switch holds for every session of the same Claude Code configuration directory and takes
   effect within 10 seconds.
2. Keep at least one session with PaceLine open, busy or idle. usage-watch reads the account's usage
   every 125 seconds while a session is open. It needs a claude.ai login.
3. To let pace account for a model's own weekly limit, pass the model with `--model`, or set
   `PACELINE_MODEL`.

**How to tell it worked:** `/paceline:usage-watch status` shows a recent `last success` and `last
error: none`. `/paceline:pace status` shows a data age of a few minutes at most, and `paceline
status --json` lists the model-scoped buckets under `weekly.scoped`. If nothing shows, see
[usage-watch shows nothing](troubleshooting.md#usage-watch-shows-nothing).

## Use two accounts on one machine

**When you need it:** you sign in to more than one Claude account on this computer and want pace to
show the limits of the account you use now.

**Which setup:** use one configuration directory and `/login` when you use one account at a time.
The same holds when Claude Code Desktop is on one account and a terminal on the other: each session
files its readings under the account of its own credential, which PaceLine asks Claude Code for, so
each session shows its own figures; so does a `claude` started from a Desktop terminal tab. A
`paceline` command outside any session takes the account of the last terminal `/login`, and
`paceline status` then ends with `other account <8 digits> active; --account <8 digits>` while
another account has a fresh reading; `paceline status --account <8 digits>` shows its figures.
PaceLine keeps each account's readings in a partition of its own, and pace reads the partition of
the account signed in now. Use a configuration directory per account (`CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR`) when two
terminal sessions on different accounts run at the same time, or when each needs its own profile
(each account already has its own week plan). See [Each configuration directory keeps its own
state](limitations.md#each-configuration-directory-keeps-its-own-state).

1. Update with `/plugin marketplace update agentpit` and restart every open session. A session still
   on PaceLine 0.2.5 does not tag its readings and mixes the accounts until it restarts.
2. Do not run `/login` during an unattended run. Stint stops the run with `account changed during
   the run`.
3. Run `/login` and sign in to the other account.
4. Run `/paceline:pace status`. It shows the new account's figures at once when that account has a
   partition from an earlier session. Otherwise it stops with `no usage data yet for the signed-in
   account` until the first reply in a session signed in to that account, or until the next
   usage-watch reading, which comes at most 125 seconds after the last one.

**How to tell it worked:** `status` does not end with `account unknown`, and `paceline status
--json` shows `data.account.state` as `known`. A `/login` back to the first account shows its last
figures at once.

**What the messages mean:**

- `no usage data yet for the signed-in account`: the signed-in account has no readings yet. It fills
  after the first reply in a session with PaceLine loaded.
- `account unknown (<reason>)`: PaceLine cannot tell that the figures belong to the session's
  account. The reason is `untagged`, `no-file`, `unreadable`, `no-account`, `no-credential`, or
  `no-state-key`. While the account is `pending` (the first seconds of a session), or not known for
  the reason `desktop` or `logged-out`, pace shows no figures. See [Status says account
  unknown](troubleshooting.md#status-says-account-unknown).
- After an update from 0.2.5, the figures show `account unknown (untagged)` until the account's
  first tagged reading arrives.

## Turn on the memory guard

**When you need it:** a heavy process on this machine, such as a test run, a container or a large
build, can use up free memory and crash the host, and you want PaceLine to ask before a launch and
to stop unattended work while free memory is low.

1. Turn the guard on. It is off by default: while it is off, PaceLine does not measure memory before
   a launch and no memory floor applies.

   ```
   paceline profile set memory_guard true
   ```

2. Set the floor and the heavy-run keys to fit the machine. They are used only while the guard is
   on; the defaults are 2048, 2048, 6000 and 3. For example, a 4 GiB floor and at most two heavy
   runs:

   ```
   paceline profile set min_free_commit_mb 4096
   paceline profile set max_heavy_runs 2
   ```

   The [profile keys](reference.md#profile-keys) say what each key does.

**How to tell it worked:** With free memory below `min_free_commit_mb`, an Agent or Workflow launch
asks first and `paceline advice` says stop to unattended work. `paceline status` says `host memory
unknown` when memory cannot be measured while the guard is on. `paceline profile set memory_guard
false` turns the guard off again. To check it, run `paceline status --json`: `"guard": true` under
`host` means the guard is on.

## Change a profile setting

**When you need it:** the budget counts in the wrong time zone, or a limit in the profile does not
fit your machine. Your working hours are part of the week plan; see [Plan a week](#plan-a-week).

1. Look at the current values. `/paceline:settings` shows every setting and switch: a summary with
   the three switches, a table for each group, a `●` before each value that differs from its
   default, and the count of Advanced settings that differ, and `/paceline:settings pane` opens a
   pane where you edit a value and save it with the same checks as `paceline profile set`; its
   Calendar tab plans the week (see [Plan a week](#plan-a-week)). The PaceLine button opens the same
   pane, and a second click closes it: in the CLI `[ PaceLine ]` follows PitBoard's button at the
   end of PitBoard's row, and in Desktop `[ PaceLine ]` sits in the footer under the prompt; without
   PitBoard the CLI has no such button. In a session where PaceLine's hooks module does not run, or
   in a plain terminal, `paceline settings` prints the same list as text. The pane is read-only on a
   phone. A new skill needs a new session in Claude Code Desktop, so start one after you update
   PaceLine:

   ```
   /paceline:settings
   /paceline:settings pane
   ```

2. Change one key. The value is read as JSON when it parses, else as text:

   ```
   paceline profile set timezone America/New_York
   paceline profile set max_agents 4
   paceline profile set five_hour_stop_pct 90
   paceline profile set min_free_commit_mb 1024
   ```

   Set these first: `timezone` and, if you turn on the memory guard, its floor (`min_free_commit_mb`
   and `commit_reserve_mb`; see [Turn on the memory guard](#turn-on-the-memory-guard)). The defaults
   for the floor are starting points and count only while the guard is on. If a confirmation prompt
   about free memory appears at most Agent launches, lower `min_free_commit_mb`. The working hours
   are not a profile key; see [Plan a week](#plan-a-week).
3. A new profile follows this machine's time zone, so it moves when the machine does. To count in a
   fixed zone instead, for example a team's zone, run `paceline profile set timezone Europe/Kyiv`:
   it also turns the mode to `fixed`. `paceline profile set timezone_mode machine` follows the
   machine again. To keep `UTC` while this machine is in another zone, run `paceline profile set
   timezone UTC`. That also silences the time zone hint at session start. A profile created by an
   earlier version stays fixed until you choose the machine mode.

**How to tell it worked:** `profile set` prints `KEY: OLD -> NEW` and the new `paceline status`
line, for example `max_agents: 6 -> 4`; the pane shows the same line in a message after a save. A
refused value exits 2, prints the reason, and changes nothing. The [profile
keys](reference.md#profile-keys) list what each key does and its range. `five_hour_stop_pct` (95 by
default) is the five-hour usage from which a launch asks you first, in working hours and off-hours
alike. The reserve is set with `paceline reserve` (see [Keep a reserve for a task at the end of the
week](#keep-a-reserve-for-a-task-at-the-end-of-the-week)).

## Seat PaceLine as your organization's plugin

**When you need it:** your organization manages Claude Code (a Team or Enterprise login, or a
machine with managed settings) and you want the plugins' hooks modules to see every event. Claude
Code's `sec-default` guard withholds the `classic.*` events and `session.compact` from the hooks
module of a plugin you install yourself, but not from a plugin the organization's managed settings
load from an administrator-only folder. PaceLine's own module uses none of the withheld events, so
PaceLine runs in full under the guard. The seating still matters for PitBoard, whose compaction
event the guard withholds (see [Where an organization manages Claude Code, PitBoard sees a
compaction
late](../../pitboard/docs/limitations.md#where-an-organization-manages-claude-code-pitboard-sees-a-compaction-late)),
and, from the release that adds it, for PitCrew's context-watch. Seating it there relaxes the
organization's security settings, so it fits a small team whose owner decides that, and hardly a
large organization.

One script per platform seats PaceLine and PitBoard together. It fetches each plugin from the public
agentpit repository at its release tag, copies it into an administrator-only folder, writes a
managed settings file that enables it there, and disables your own copies, `paceline@agentpit` and
`pitboard@agentpit`. It never edits an existing `managed-settings.json`. dbWise needs none of this:
the guard leaves its hooks alone.

1. Where the organization has server-managed settings (claude.ai, Organization settings > Claude
   Code > Managed settings), add `"managedSourcesBehavior": "merge"` there. Without it Claude Code
   ignores the plugin keys of this machine's managed file, and with your own copies disabled neither
   plugin loads.
2. On Windows, download
   [Install-AgentpitOrg.ps1](https://github.com/agentpit-lab/agentpit/blob/main/tools/Install-AgentpitOrg.ps1)
   and run it in PowerShell 7 as an administrator:

   ```
   pwsh -NoProfile -File .\Install-AgentpitOrg.ps1
   ```

3. On macOS or Linux, download
   [install-agentpit-org.sh](https://github.com/agentpit-lab/agentpit/blob/main/tools/install-agentpit-org.sh)
   and run it as yourself; it calls `sudo` where it writes system folders. It is tested on Windows
   and Linux, not yet on macOS.

   ```
   sh install-agentpit-org.sh
   ```

   In a terminal the script lists the last ten releases of each plugin with the latest selected, and
   Enter keeps it. `-Version pitboard=0.1.14` (`--version` in sh) pins a release; `-Latest`
   (`--latest`) takes the latest of both without asking, as a run without a terminal does.
   Unreleased builds install only from a local folder with `-Source` (`--source`).

   The script writes two paths. Windows: `C:\Program Files\ClaudeCode\plugins\agentpit-org` and
   `C:\Program Files\ClaudeCode\managed-settings.d\50-agentpit-org.json`. macOS: the same two under
   `/Library/Application Support/ClaudeCode/`. Linux: `/opt/claude-code/plugins/agentpit-org` and
   `/etc/claude-code/managed-settings.d/50-agentpit-org.json`.
4. Restart every Claude Code session.

**How to tell it worked:** `claude --debug` logs `hooks module paceline@agentpit-org loaded` with
`tier append`, and no line says `bypassed by`. `claude plugin list` does not show a plugin loaded in
place from a managed folder.

To update, run the script again. To undo, run it with `-Uninstall` (`--uninstall`): it removes the
folder and the managed file and enables your own copies again. The managed file applies to every
login on the machine, a personal one included, and seats the guard there too: another plugin with a
hooks module that you install from a marketplace loses the same events on that login.
